summary: Iteration 3 regression verification of the two refactored N+1->batched endpoints (POST /api/v1/cart/sync and GET /api/v1/kits) plus a state-independent rewrite of TestStreakRewards. All 34 pytests pass under the default parallel config (-n 2 --dist loadscope) and serially. Cart/sync: with 3 valid product ids + 1 unknown id + one qty above stockQuantity, response contains only the 3 valid items, the over-qty item is clamped to stockQuantity, unitPrice==salePrice and lineTotal==qty*unitPrice for each item, itemTotal==sum(lineTotals); empty items -> [] and itemTotal 0; all-unknown items -> [] and itemTotal 0. Kits: GET /kits returns 6 fully-resolved kits (each item has product.sku/title/salePrice/mrp), itemCount==sum(quantities), kitPrice==round(sum(salePrice*qty)), mrpTotal==round(sum(mrp*qty)), savings==mrpTotal-kitPrice; GET /kits/kit-class10 returns 7 items; GET /kits/unknown -> 404. Streak tests: rewritten to read the persisted streak first and assert discountPercent==min(3+streak,10); the increment test now uses a dedicated `streak-test-user` to avoid a parallel-execution race against test_kapa_api::TestOrders which posts orders on userId=guest.

minor.issue: Increments the streak counter for ANY user whose exam date is active whenever a study-category product is ordered. Under pytest-xdist loadscope this caused a cross-module race between test_kapa_api::TestOrders (creates orders on userId=guest) and test_kapa_iteration2::TestStreakRewards (had exam active for guest). Fixed on the test side by using a dedicated userId in the increment test. Not a product bug, but worth flagging: any future test that leaves an exam active on `guest` and orders study products will drift the counter.
Does not reset the `streak` field, only $unsets examName/examDate. Streak persists across exam cycles (already flagged in iteration_2, still holds). Confirmed live: guest streak is 7 after this run.

action_items: None blocking - refactor is verified. Optional: reset `streak` to 0 in DELETE /api/v1/rewards/exam-date if a fresh 3% baseline is desired after an exam cycle ends.
Optional: consider scoping order-side streak side-effects to authenticated users (or a header-provided userId) so shared 'guest' state is less race-prone across tests.

Two known cross-module shared-state pitfalls under `userId=guest`: (a) order creation increments streak when an exam is active; (b) address seeding auto-promotes Home to default. Use unique userIds when writing new tests that mutate rewards. Refactored endpoints of interest: server.py:367-388 (cart/sync $in) and server.py:519-537 (kits batched products_by_sku).
